climate: warm humid summers, mild winters; MAP 1368 mm, MAT 14.8 C
cover_crop: five-species mix (soil health mix: cereal rye, crimson clover, hairy vetch, daikon radish, oat)
comparison: five-species CC mix vs. other CC treatments and winter fallow (no CC, no herbicide)
uncertainty: range 6 to 8.5% depending on comparison treatment
n: 4 replicates; 2 soybean years (2014, 2016); no-till corn-soybean rotation
quote: A five-species CC mixture increased soybean yields by 6 to 8.5% across seeding method treat- ments compared with other CC treatments and winter fallow.
note: Upper bound 8.5%. Increase significant only in drought year 2016. Quote contains a line-break hyphen ('treat- ments') as in the extracted text.

climate: warm humid summers, mild winters; MAP 1368 mm, MAT 14.8 C
cover_crop: five-species mix vs. single/double-species CC and fallow
comparison: soybean yield after five-species mix (3.5) vs. other CC treatments and winter fallow (3.2-3.28)
uncertainty: other treatments incl. fallow 3.2-3.28 Mg ha-1; P = 0.019 for CC type effect
quote: Across the 2 yr (2014, 2016) and planting methods (drilling and broadcasting), soy- bean planted after multi-species SHM had a significantly higher yield (3.5 Mg ha−1) than planted after all other CC treatments and the CTRL (3.2–3.28 Mg ha−1; Figure 6).
note: Wheat, cereal rye, rye/clover, rye/vetch did not differ from fallow (Figure 6). Quote contains a line-break hyphen ('soy- bean').

climate: warm humid summers, mild winters; MAP 1368 mm, MAT 14.8 C
cover_crop: any (wheat, cereal rye, rye/clover, rye/vetch, five-species mix)
metric: corn grain yield range across CC types (no significant effect)
quote: Cover crop types had no significant effect on corn yield (P > .05; Table 2) with mean yields ranging from 14.1 to 15 Mg ha−1 across the CC types.
note: Corn years had normal/adequate rainfall; authors interpret as neutral CC effect on corn.

climate: warm humid summers, mild winters; MAP 1368 mm, MAT 14.8 C
comparison: broadcast-seeded CC vs. drilled CC (planting method moderator)
quote: However, CC planting method had a significant effect on corn yield (P ≤.05), whereas the broadcast-seeded CC exhibited significantly higher corn yields (15.1 Mg ha−1) than the drilled CC (14.3 Mg ha−1).
note: Moderator result (seeding method), not CC vs. no CC. Planting method had no effect on soybean yield.
